assessment.overall_rationale: The replicates strongly agree on the enzymatic cholesterol-biosynthesis module, but their matched regulatory and VLDL-coupling narratives contain explicit reversals in predicted knockout effects despite sharing the same molecular components.

pair_scores.rationale: Both modules describe the same near-complete mevalonate-to-cholesterol enzyme cascade in hepatocytes with essentially identical pathway output and genes.
The modules concern the same cholesterol-synthesis program, but one is the enzymatic pathway while the other is its upstream SREBP2 sterol-sensing control circuit.
Both center on hepatic mevalonate and cholesterol synthesis, although the right module emphasizes pathological elevation, senescence, and VLDL-related regulation rather than pathway execution.
The SREBP2 feedback circuit directly controls the enzymatic pathway described on the right, but regulator control and metabolic execution are distinct mechanisms.
Both identify the same SCAP–INSIG1–SREBP2–LDLR circuit, but they explicitly predict opposite effects of Scap and Insig1 knockout on program activity.
Both connect SREBP-mediated sterol regulation to hepatic cholesterol synthesis, but the right module shifts toward MASLD, aging, senescence, and VLDL disruption.
Both involve hepatic cholesterol synthesis, but the left module specifically asserts coupling to triglyceride-loaded VLDL assembly and secretion.
VLDL output and SREBP2 sterol sensing intersect through cholesterol demand, but the modules focus on different regulators, mechanisms, and predicted phenotypes.
Both invoke Dgat2/Mttp-dependent VLDL export in MASLD and aging, but one says impaired export attenuates sterol synthesis whereas the other says it activates and amplifies it.
